entries.reason: REQ-SPEC — All five spec requirements are implemented in the diff. R1: merge.js adds `runGit(['-C', mainRepoPath, 'checkout', baseBranch])` before `runSquashMerge`, ensuring the squash commit lands on baseBranch even when the main repo is on a different branch. R2: when checkout fails, a temporary detached worktree is created via `git worktree add --detach`, squash-merged there, and `git update-ref` advances baseBranch only after success; if any step throws, baseBranch is left unchanged. R3: the temporary worktree removal is in a `finally` block, guaranteeing cleanup on both success and failure paths. R4: git-helpers.js inspects `res.stderr` with `/unstaged changes|uncommitted changes/` and returns `{ reason: 'dirty', conflictFiles: [], ... }` for dirty failures and `{ reason: 'conflict', conflictFiles, ... }` for real conflicts. R5: runPreSync checks `rebaseRes.reason === 'dirty'` and returns `recoveryHint: 'Pre-merge rebase failed: working tree has uncommitted changes. Commit or discard changes in the worktree before retrying finalize.'` — matching the spec-mandated string exactly, with no mention of stash.; No Hardcoded Secrets — No API keys, passwords, tokens, or other secrets appear in the added lines. The test fixtures use only dummy git config values (t@example.com, 'T') which are clearly non-sensitive test data.; No Silent Error Swallowing — In the finally block added to merge.js, `runGit(["-C", mainRepoPath, "worktree", "remove", "--force", tmpWorktree])` is called but its return value is completely discarded. If the worktree removal fails, the error is silently swallowed with no logging or re-throw. This is especially problematic because spec requirement R3 mandates the temporary worktree be deleted on both success and failure — a silent failure here violates both the guardrail and the requirement.; No Sensitive Data in Logs — No log statements in the added lines write passwords, tokens, or personally identifiable information. Error messages reference git command output and branch names only.; No Disabling Existing Tests — No existing tests are skipped, commented out, or deleted anywhere in the diff. Only new test files and spec artifacts are added.; Escalate Pre-Existing Test Failures — Determining whether tests were already failing before this diff requires runtime test execution, which is not available from the static diff content.; Spec Test Coverage — All five requirements (R1–R5) defined in spec.json have corresponding test cases in specs/248-merge-checkout-and-rebase-error/tests/248-merge-checkout.test.js, and the test-map.json correctly cross-references each requirement to its test(s).; Project Test Integrity — The diff changes rebaseOnto's return shape for failure cases from `{ ok: false, conflictFiles, stderr }` to `{ ok: false, reason, conflictFiles, stderr }`. The file tests/unit/lib/git-sync-helpers.test.js (mentioned explicitly in spec-review.md as asserting the old shape) is not updated in this diff. If those tests use strict equality assertions on the return value, they will fail after this change is merged, violating the requirement that all project tests pass.; Code Placement — The new logic is placed in the modules that own the relevant responsibility: rebaseOnto's dirty-worktree detection belongs in git-helpers.js (the git abstraction layer), and the squash-merge routing belongs in merge.js. The added `set` method on Container is within the container module itself. No cross-module placement violations are introduced by the diff.; Exit Code Contract — No new CLI commands are added or modified. All changes are to internal library functions (merge.js worktree route, git-helpers.js rebaseOnto). Exit code behavior at the CLI boundary is not affected.; No Synchronous I/O in Hot Paths — The added source code in merge.js and git-helpers.js contains no synchronous I/O calls (readFileSync, writeFileSync, etc.) in loops or bulk-processing paths. Test-file usage of fs.writeFileSync is in test setup/teardown only, not in production hot paths.; Validate User Input at Entry Point — No new CLI commands or user-facing arguments are introduced by this diff. The changes are entirely to internal merge and rebase helper functions, so no new entry-point validation is required.
